## Release v1.0.4

Compare changes: https://github.com/lenucksi/opencode-pty/compare/v1.0.3...v1.0.4

- Release 1.0.4 (67e6cc0)
- The exit tag now travels as data, not as a live object (30d385c)
- A cold start no longer waits for a daemon that is already up (3185fc8)
- The mark is a prompt, and a second cursor (b1598a3)
- Eight marks, and the favicon is a reduction of its own (58e4a6c)
- The notice carries the copyright lines, and each licence body once (6685cf5)
- The interface has a brand, and a status line that is always there (de3f988)
- The patch stays a maintainer artefact, not a shipped one (98795da)

### Installation

Add to your `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["opencode-pty"]
}
```

### Update Instructions

To get the latest version:

```bash
rm -rf ~/.cache/opencode/node_modules/opencode-pty
opencode
```

## Release v1.0.3

Compare changes: https://github.com/lenucksi/opencode-pty/compare/v1.0.1...v1.0.3

- Releases are staged, and a human approves them (ca4ebd3)
- Release 1.0.2, for the trusted publisher's validation window (0f864a7)

### Installation

Add to your `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["opencode-pty"]
}
```

### Update Instructions

To get the latest version:

```bash
rm -rf ~/.cache/opencode/node_modules/opencode-pty
opencode
```

First published release of the fork, as **`@lenucksi/agentterm`** (the npm name
`opencode-pty` belongs to the upstream project). The plugin id, the daemon socket,
the state directory and the storage keys keep the old name on purpose: renaming
them would strand a running daemon and orphan the archive.

### Added

**Named keys, quiet waits, and an installer with both edges**

- `pty_sendkey` sends a key by name - `Enter`, `Tab`, `Escape`, arrows,
  `Home`/`End`/`PageUp`/`PageDown`, `C-a`..`C-z`, `F1`..`F12` - with `times` to
  repeat. `pty_write` makes a model spell bytes, and a wrong byte is not an error,
  it is a prompt that does not move. A name the terminal does not have is refused
  with the list of names that exist; a command still goes through `pty_write`,
  where the permission policy sees it.
- `pty_wait` takes `quietMs`: return once the session has printed nothing for that
  long, with the process still running. That is how a prompt is awaited without a
  `pty_read` loop. The result says which ending it had (`reason="quiet"` or
  `"exit"`), and a quiet one has no `Exit:` line, because there is no exit status.
- `agentterm-mcp install` prints the two edges this package is reached through:
  the OpenCode plugin entry (the one file `--write` touches, merging into the
  existing `plugin` array with a `.bak` first) and the MCP server block for
  everything else (`mcpServers`, `claude mcp add`, or a printed TOML block for
  Codex). Nothing is written without `--write`.

**Third-party notices in the docs dialog**

The Docs dialog has a third tab, _Licences_. It lists every installed package
grouped by licence, with the package count per group and `name@version` under it,
plus four credits lines for the projects this repository is built on. The package
data is generated at build time from `bun pm licenses --json` into
`dist/licenses.json` and served by `GET /api/licenses`, so the tab cannot fall out
of step with the lockfile. The artifact is sorted and stripped of paths and other
machine metadata, which makes a rebuild on an unchanged lockfile byte-identical.

**Rolling the daemon from both surfaces**

The daemon is machine state that every OpenCode instance on the machine shares:
one socket, one pid file, one process that owns every PTY. Until now the only
way to roll it was the `/pty-daemon-restart` command, and only the server half
answered it - so a surface that is not the server could not ask.

There is now one roll, reachable from everywhere:

- the **TUI sidebar footer** grows a second line, `daemon · restart`, with the
  pid of the daemon that answered the last roll. Clicking it rolls the daemon;
  the line says `daemon · restarting…` while the roll runs and the result
  arrives as a toast.
- the **web interface** gets a _Restart the daemon_ button in the settings,
  with the answer next to the button. The button is disabled while a roll runs:
  two rolls at once are how a machine ends up with two daemons.

Both ask the half that owns the client - the server half, over the plugin's own
RPC and over `POST /api/daemon/restart` respectively - because the daemon
belongs to the server, not to the surface that asks.

A roll ends every session the daemon owns: the PTY masters belong to that
process. The archive on disk survives.

Every roll is announced to every surface, marked with the id of the action that
started it. The surface that started it recognises its own mark and stays quiet (it
already shows the answer); every other one shows it. So a roll from the browser
reaches the TUI's sidebar, and the other way round.

The sidebar's line now shows the **running** daemon's pid, refreshed by the panel's
poll rather than only by its own roll, so a roll started anywhere is visible there
within a tick.

**Toasts in the web interface**

The web interface shows what the server half says: a slash command's result, a roll
started in another surface. The notice arrives over the WebSocket the page already
holds, with the same shape t

## [0.7.1] - 2026-10-17

### Fixed

**The TUI session panel draws the colours the program used**

The panel rendered a session's screen as plain text, so a program that paints - the
UEFI boot menu, `ls --color`, `htop` - arrived in black and white while the same
session was coloured in the web UI. The colour was never missing on the wire: the
server's screen render already resolved every cell's foreground, background and
attributes. It was dropped twice on the way to the panel - once when the decoder
kept only the rows, and once when the renderer drew one plain string.

The response now carries `styledLines`: the same runs as `spans`, but as text, so a
consumer without a terminal of its own can place the characters (a wide character is
one character and two cells, which is why cell coordinates alone were not enough).
The panel draws one `<text>` per run in a row box. Background padding survives - the
boot menu's blue box is a run of spaces carrying a background - while plain trailing
padding is still trimmed.

## [0.7.0] - 2026-10-17

### Added

**`raw` spawn option for PTY sessions**

`pty_spawn` and the session-creation API accept `raw: true`, which disables the
PTY slave's line discipline (`stty raw -echo`) before the command runs. Use it for
a serial console (`virsh console`), a boot menu, or any program that expects a
`\r` to stay a `\r`.

Without it, the kernel's cooked discipline applies ICRNL and delivers Enter as
`\n`. A libvirt serial console showed its boot menu and relayed arrow keys, but
Enter did nothing - the byte was written and the program never saw it. Arrow keys
are escape sequences and are not translated, which is why only Enter was affected.
Raw mode turns ICRNL, ICANON, ISIG and ECHO off, so bytes arrive verbatim. It is
opt-in because a shell would lose line editing and the interrupt key.

`pty_list` and the `<pty_spawned>` result now report whether a session is raw.

### Fixed

- Enter works on a serial console reached through `pty_spawn`: the new `raw` option
  stops the line discipline from rewriting a carriage return into a line feed.
